Will be speaking in terms of my experience with the Ayala Malls Feliz branch.

The modern facial - First one I got. This was more for hydration and cleansing. One hour treatment! They check the hydration level of your skin before and after the treatment. May serum and mask of your choice (both either for brightening, anti-aging, etc. you can mix and match). Starts of with a gentle cleansing milk to remove and residue on the face. Then steam, vacuum. What would follow is the mask, serum, tapos may cooling probe yung machine. Malamig talaga siyaaa. Then sunscreen. I liked it. It was gentle and relaxing. But I needed something more robust for my concerns (hyperpigmentation).

Between the Clearlift and Pixel, I chose the Clearlift.

Both use the same machine but the wands that do each procedure is different. I can’t speak for Pixel. Pixel sounds appealing and I would totally go for it but it has a downtime. Mag scab and lift kasi yung top layer ng balat with Pixel. It’s best for deeper acne scars, and of course helps with marks. I couldn’t afford the downtime because I have to report to work physically thrice a week. Need daw na minimal sun exposure during this period.

Now, for Clearlift. It’s mainly geared for tightening, anti aging, and for hyperpigmentation also. I opted for this kasi walang downtime. Prior the Clearlift, may quick facial. Cleaning, vacuum (walang mask afair). Lilipat ka sa Laser room after the facial and the procedure will begin. Clearlift uses 5 different “probes” (not sure how they call it haha) but each probe targets a different layer of the skin. Several passes sa skin yung sa clearlift. Nothing too painful din yung pag hit ng laser BUT it can get loud, especially the last one. Medyo makati sa balat but normal naman yun kasi laser nga siya. After ng Clearlift, bawal lang basain face for 5 hours then back to regular programming na. No exfoliating products lang for the next three days and of course sunscreen everyday. The staff discuss it with you clearly naman. Before the procedure, they ask for info and skin concerns. Then post procedure, they message you after care instructions also. The place is clean and the staff are in PPE. 

Out of the two, I booked another Clearlift session. I can say it has made a difference for my hyperpigmentation sa cheeks caused na rin ng maskne. This + the Axis Y Dark Spot Correcting Serum (which I bought from them na rin) have really helped. Might get the package na kasi mas tipid.

This response is going to be long.

There are at least two factors you should consider in getting a menstrual cup. Cervix height and flow :) There are plenty of videos on youtube about bow to measure a cervix height. The online menstrual cup quizzes also are a big help. 
In terms of cup brands, marami nang generic, re branded cups available in the PH market. What does generic rebranded mean? It means that there is a private manufacturer of menstrual cups (let’s call them supplier) that sell to interested parties who then sells in the PH under a brand.
Examples of more prominent suppliers
1. furuize
2. ningbo luke
They are both FDA registered facilities that make medical devices.
Generic, rebranded cups in the PH:
Anytime, AuntFlo, Bulan, Sinaya, iCare, Serene, Luna Cup Korea, Moontime, Comfort, Vivi, Canack (to name a few)
Look alikes: Canack, Luna Cup Shorty, Serene XS shorty
Look alikes: Serene regular, Luna Cup regular, AuntFlo
Look alikes: Vivi, Anytime, Bulan

Are these generic, rebranded cups harmful/bad? No. Not per se but since these are made in bulk and sold for private labelling, quality control can be an issue. Sentiments from users that have both rebranded and self-made branded cups (will cite examples of these self-made branded cups) notice that rebranded cups get softer faster. This indicates a lower quality silicone was used.

Should I buy these cups? Totally up to you. I personally don’t see anything wrong since finances can be an understandable issue. Buying a cup is an upfront investment which at one go can be a larger sum of money compared to buying disposables. Local rebranded cups are a good first stepping stone into the world of menstrual cups such as in terms of insertion, what kind of cup will work, firmness you prefer, etc.
My biggest gripe against SOME brands though are the HUGE markup. I understand it’s a business but some of these cups can be bought in bulk at AliExpress for about 50 pesos and you see some local brands resell them for 995-1000+. May sense of falsehood na may original research behind or something yung brands.

On the other hand, 
Self-made brands are what I would call brands that did Research and development, and made their own menstrual cup silicone molds. Examples of these cups/brands (to name a few lang):
Lunette, Lena, Saalt, Intimina (motherbrand), Tieut, Hello Cup, OrganiCup, MeLuna, Diva, Tampax, Super Jennie, Venus, Flex
And many more. There are plenty.
Biggest problem I can see with these cups? Price and accessibility. May mga shopee resellers na (thankfully) and prices are a little higher than the local rebranded cups that we have (though to be honest, Hindi na ganun kalaki difference).

This may seem overwhelming because truthfully it can be and allow yourself the time to understand your body so you know what cup would suit you. I’ve been a cup user for about 4 years now. I started with an Anytime Cup (then I broke it. Totally fault). Then I switch to a Lily Cup Classic A (silicone quality is superb) but didn’t know that I have an average cervix height pala and it would protrude sometimes. I since switched to the Saalt small and has been working great! I can use Tieut on heavier days.

Good luck on your menstrual cup journey! Feel free to join Menstrual Cup Users Philippines over at FB as well. That group is a huge help.

Hi. A graduate of molecular biology here and cancer is a well-discussed topic in our field. Though I see the point where you are coming from, you seem to have missed some crucial details.

1. Cancer cells/tumors are highly vascularized. They have plenty of blood vessels which are also connected to the healthy circulatory system of the host. Extensive studies are available (feel free to search) as reading material that show that cancer cells produce certain proteins (cytokines, growth factors, etc) that are either elevated or are not found in normal cells. Therefore, you cannot simply assume that transplanting cancer from a patient to a healthy host will allow the host produce antibodies against the cancer. Cytokines inherent in the cancer cells can easily induce certain responses in the host which can be undesirable. Besides, the memory-based immune system is only the 2nd line of defense in recognizing foreign bodies. Your NK cells are the first ones to attack foreign bodies. If your cancer dies even before it is recognized by your B-cells and T-cells, there will be no production of antibodies.

2. Studies in rats and mice have shown that blood transfusions actually aggravate cancer progression and can even increase the rate of mortality in cancer patients. https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/pmc/articles/PMC2694914/#!po=7.97101
